The '''All Terrain Riot Control Transport (AT-RCT)''' was a model of [[AT-series/Legends|All Terrain]] [[Walker/Legends|walker]] manufactured by [[Kuat Drive Yards/Legends|Kuat Drive Yards]] for the intended roles of crowd control and riot suppression in urban areas. Introduced in the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], it was based on the [[All Terrain Recon Transport/Legends|All Terrain Recon Transport]] and deployed by the [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|Grand Army of the Republic]] during the [[Battle of Kashyyyk/Legends|Battle of Kashyyyk]]. After the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the AT-RCT was used by the [[Imperial Army/Legends|Imperial Army]] and the [[Law enforcement agency/Legends|police forces]] of [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], as well as many [[Planet/Legends|planetary]] and [[Star system/Legends|system]] governments. A revised iteration of the walker was later used by [[Darth Krayt's Galactic Empire]] during the [[Second Imperial Civil War]].

==Characteristics==
[[File:Openair_atst.jpg|thumb|left|140px|An early AT-RCT on [[Kashyyyk/Legends|Kashyyyk]].]]
The walker was open-topped, like the [[All Terrain Recon Transport/Legends|All Terrain Recon Transport]] model, but larger in scale.<ref name="Legacy Era Campaign Guide" /> It had room for two [[Pilot/Legends|pilots]].

==History==
An early version of the walker was in service in the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic's]] [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|Grand Army of the Republic]]. These walkers participated in the [[Battle of Kashyyyk/Legends|Battle of Kashyyyk]] in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]].<ref name="RotS 3" /> Two were later deployed alongside a clone detachment to the [[Colonies/Legends|Colonies]] world of [[Kestavel]], to apprehend the Jedi fugitive [[Dass Jennir]] during the Great Jedi Purge of the early events of the Galactic Empire.<ref name="A Spark Remains 1" /> The type saw increased use in the [[Fel Empire]] and [[Darth Krayt's Galactic Empire]], over 150 years later.<ref name="Legacy Era Campaign Guide" />

==Behind the scenes==
The All Terrain Riot Control Transport was originally created for the [[2005]] film [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']], though it was cut from the final film. Designed by [[T.J. Frame]], it was dubbed the "Twin AT-ST"<ref name="ArtStation">{{ArtStation|username=tjframe|url=artwork/z1LAQ|name=TJ Frame|text=3D Work done for the 2005 film Star Wars: Episode III - Revenge of The Sith}}</ref> and, in a [[Ryan Church]] concept piece done on [[June 13]], [[2003]], would have appeared alongside an AT-RT and [[Infantry Support Platform/Legends|Infantry Support Platform]] in a scene where [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]] was found by a searchlight that was mounted below an AT-RCT's central cannons<ref name="The Art of RotS">''[[The Art of Star Wars Episode III: Revenge of the Sith]]''</ref> and distracted mutinous [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone troopers]] by acting like a crazy hermit. [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]] would have then climbed up the back of the AT-RT and removed the pilot, reminiscent of his boarding of an [[All Terrain Scout Transport/Legends|All Terrain Scout Transport]] in the [[1983]] film [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']].<ref name="AT-RT">{{DB|vehicle|atrt|All Terrain Recon Transport (AT-RT walker)}}</ref>

Though omitted from the film itself, the "Twin AT-ST" appeared in the [[Star Wars: Episode III — Revenge of the Sith 3|third issue]] of Episode III's [[Star Wars: Episode III — Revenge of the Sith (comic series)|comic adaptation]] written by [[Christopher Cerasi]] under the pseudonym Miles Lane,<ref name="Epic Collection">''[[Star Wars Legends Epic Collection: The Clone Wars Vol. 4]]''</ref> pencilled by [[Douglas Wheatley]],<ref name="RotS 3" /> and published on [[April 13]], 2005.<ref name="RotS 3 release date">{{Marvel|url=comics/issue/54230/star_wars_episode_iii_-_revenge_of_the_sith_2005_3|text=Star Wars: Episode III - Revenge of the Sith (2005) #3}}</ref> Its design was later repurposed as the All Terrain Riot Control Transport in the ''[[Legacy Era Campaign Guide]]'', a [[2009]] supplement for [[Wizards of the Coast]]'s ''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game]]''. While the walker was described as having been based upon vehicle designs dating back to the Clone Wars,<ref name="Legacy Era Campaign Guide" /> the "Twin AT-ST" was not identified as an earlier model of AT-RCT until the publication of ''[[Far Horizons]]'', a [[2014]] supplement for [[Fantasy Flight Games]]' ''[[Star Wars: Edge of the Empire]]'' [[roleplaying game]].<ref name="Far Horizons" />
